sara_marketing: Quick heads-up: this morning we saw a burst where ~9% of new HubSpot leads weren't claimed within our 2m SLA. Pattern looks like enrichment timeouts blocking the RR claim step.
sara_marketing: Examples: leads 55123, 55127, 55142. Enrichment returned 504 or very long tails.
jason_revops: Thanks. Can you paste one full workflow log for 55123? want to see retries and timestamps.
sara_marketing: pasted snippet: `2026-03-21T09:12:01Z inbound -> enrichment triggered -> 09:12:01Z enrichment call 1 (timeout 30s) -> 09:12:32Z workflow paused waiting for enrichment -> 09:18:35Z claim attempted (owner null)`
alex_salesops: Proposed: stop blocking claim on enrichment. Two options: 1) optimistic claim immediately with temporary owner flag, reconcile on enrichment completion; or 2) claim to a shared fallback queue within 30s. Prefer optimistic claim + jitter to reduce races.
emily_sales: If we optimistic-claim, make sure SF sync only pushes final owner once enrichment completes or fallback triggers. Otherwise reps see churn in Salesforce.
tia_eng: Implementation plan from infra: add enrichment "fast-pending" status when enrichment latency > 2s or on known upstream issues. Workflow will interpret "fast-pending" as non-blocking. Feature flag toggle for 10% canary. I can have a small PR today.
maria_growth: Also recommend a human-safe fallback: after 4 minutes unclaimed -> route to `inbound-ops` queue and send a Slack alert to #inbound-ops. For lead_score >= 75, page on-call.
alex_salesops: Claim jitter: when RoundRobin returns N candidates, instead of racing they will attempt to claim with an incremental random backoff 0-25s. This cuts down on spiky DB contention.
jason_revops: Metrics we need: lead.claim.latency.p50/p95/p99, lead.enrich.slow_counts, lead.claim_attempts.per_lead, lead.fallback.count. Alert if p99 > 2m or fallback_rate > 1% for leads score >= 60.
ops_bot: note: previous fallback owner was `unassigned-queue`. Suggest switching to `inbound-ops` for clearer oncall routing.
alex_salesops: Draft workflow pseudo:
```
on lead_create:
  call enrichment async (mark enrichment_status=pending)
  attempt optimistic_claim() with owner_temp and owner_source="optimistic"
  if claim success -> emit metric claimed=1
  if claimed == false and time_since_create > 240s -> route to inbound-ops and emit fallback metric

# optimistic_claim implementation does randomized sleep <=25s per candidate before trying to claim
```

emily_sales: Salesforce notes: set `owner_temp` on HubSpot side and map to a temp field in SF. Only sync `owner_final` when enrichment_status == "complete" or fallback triggers. This prevents churn and inaccurate lead reassignment notifications.
jason_revops: Acceptance criteria for rollout: after 10% canary running for 2h with no user complaints and p99 claim latency < 2m, promote to 100%. Fallback rate should be <0.5% for score>=70.
tia_eng: I'll push flag-gated change and a small enrichment-side status update. ETA: PR in next 3 hours, canary deploy tonight.
maria_growth: I'll prepare the SDR faq explaining the optimistic behavior and the temporary owner field. Will schedule message in #sales before 100% flip.
sara_marketing: Rollout checklist:
- tia: deploy enrichment status flag to canary (10%)
- alex: update HubSpot workflow + RR jitter code for canary
- jason: create dashboards and set alerts
- maria: comms to SDRs + update runbook
- emily: coordinate SF mapping for temp owner

deploy_bot: deploy scheduled: hubspot/optimistic-claim -> canary 2026-03-21T18:10Z (flag=on:10%) :rocket:

alex_salesops: I'll attach the exported HubSpot workflow JSON here after deploy.
jason_revops: Perfect. If any anomalies, we flip the flag off and revert claim flow.
emily_sales: +1. Good safety plan.
maria_growth: I'll send the SDR note and cc product and ops for visibility.
sara_marketing: Thanks everyone — let's monitor closely during the canary window.
